title: Swiss Inn Nexus Hotel | Gerji | ስዊስ ኢን ኔክሰስ ሆቴል | ገርጂ
address: Bole, Anbessa Garage, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
description: Informal lodging offering pools, dining & a rooftop bar, plus a spa with a sauna & a hot tub.

owner.name: Swiss Inn Nexus Hotel | Gerji | ስዊስ ኢን ኔክሰስ ሆቴል | ገርጂ (Owner)

user_reviews.Name: Milen Alebel
user_reviews.Description:
My boyfriend stayed at this hotel, and our experience was extremely disappointing. The rooms had mold and a bad smell, and the overall cleanliness was poor. One of the staff members stole a ring that was left on the table in the room, and the management did nothing about it.

They also charged us $20 every time I wanted to visit  my boyfriend, even though he was a registered guest. When we asked for a refund for the unused nights because of these problems, they refused.

The customer service was unhelpful and unprofessional. This hotel does not treat guests fairly and seems unsafe. I do not recommend Nexus Swiss Hotel to anyone, especially international visitors.

user_reviews.Name: Az
user_reviews.Description: I had really had bad experience! I stayed there for three weeks ! The floor in the room is dirty carpet and smells nasty! I told them to clean and they tried but it didn’t go away ! I was literally sick asa result of it ! Most importantly, the staffs need trainings how to communicate with guests nicely! They’re very rude ! The only reason I stayed there that long was just the location! I don’t recommend to anyone! It needs a reform !

user_reviews.Name: yosephg722
user_reviews.Description: Every thing was great. The room were clean and tidy. Breakfast was also good.I recommend this place. The overall it was very good.

user_reviews.Name: themwanin
user_reviews.Description: Amazing view amazing location close to the airport and very kind stuff … must go to hotel… we had some good food Adele kitchen opens till late which good

user_reviews.Name: Prashant Karthic J
user_reviews.Description: It was a great stay during my friend’s and my layover! I’d like to shout out Metages, Simegh, and Sirgut for their lovely service! They were all so friendly and very helpful.

user_reviews.Name: Jen Annandale
user_reviews.Description: The room was beautiful and clean! Some supplies were only set up for one despite it being a room for two which was mildly disappointing but overall a great stay. Dinner and breakfast buffet had variety to choose from.

user_reviews.Name: abdulazziz Mohamed
user_reviews.Description:
Hotel shuttle service is so unrealable, I was waiting good 2 hours from the airport..
The cleanlines of the hotel.is.not great, rooms has deemed lights so tjat you fo not see how dirty it is. Food is disgrace.

user_reviews.Name: Fearless59967484160
user_reviews.Description: Very good reception, food and very friendly attendants. Beautiful room and facilities. Not far from the airport. Very clean and welcoming.

title: Addissinia Hotel
address: Djibouti St Bole Sub-City, Werada 03, #172, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
description: Cosy rooms & suites in a down-to-earth hotel featuring a spa, a bar & a restaurant.

user_reviews.Name: mulugetawindsor
user_reviews.Description: I stayed for three days at Addissinia hotel in October/2025. My room was very clean , comfortable and peaceful. I received the best  customer service from the all members of the staff. I liked the breakfast, the variety of food they offered, and it was for free. I extremely appreciate the owner's willingness to help me stay past the the checkout time as my flight was at night time. She didn't charge me extra money. Thanks Addissinia.

user_reviews.Name: DailyChanged
user_reviews.Description: We love Addissinia Hotel! The management and staff are unbelievably accommodating and gracious. Always willing to help, no matter the time of day. The hotel and rooms are clean. The inside restaurant has options for breakfast, lunch, and dinner. It is very close to ADD airport. Without question, it is the most affordable option especially considering the service you receive. Thanks as always, and we look forward to next time.

user_reviews.Name: Anne Turner
user_reviews.Description: Exceptional value for money.  Really comfortable bed in a clean and spacious room with a balcony.  Staff very friendly.  Just a few things let it down for us.  Had to ask twice for toilet rolls and towels, food nothing special, city noise but you should expect that in any city centre.  All in all still great value stay

user_reviews.Name: Aislyn
user_reviews.Description: I only stayed here for one brief night due to an overnight layover, but staff was helpful, rooms/bathrooms were clean, shower had hot water and the dinner was pretty good given my midnight arrival when I wasn’t even expecting anything to be open.  Dining room was well organized and pretty. Would return

user_reviews.Name: yohannesa829
user_reviews.Description: My experience at this Hotel started from the airport. The shuttle service from and to the airport was efficient. The room is clean and spacious, booking was efficient. Breakfast was excellent with pleasant stuff attending to my needs with smile. The hotel is situated near the airport and the major attractions in the city. I would happily return in my next trip

user_reviews.Name: jes williams
user_reviews.Description: Ot wasn't really what I expected of a transit hotel from Ethiopian Airlines. Although the management were nice, some of the amenities are not working especially accessing hot water to shower.

user_reviews.Name: Fariha Aumi
user_reviews.Description: I stayed one night for transit there, their service is really good and staffs are really helpful. Room quality is cool.

user_reviews.Name: Abdibasid Khatib
user_reviews.Description: I stayed over 3 weeks and I had good time with my family. Well serviced. Nice place and nice people

title: Emmad Apartment| Hotel | ኢማድ አፓርትመንት ሆቴል
address: Ring Road, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

owner.name: Emmad Apartment| Hotel | ኢማድ አፓርትመንት ሆቴል (Owner)

user_reviews.Name: Sherpa08275612401
user_reviews.Description: I booked it through Agoda and stayed at Emmad Furnished Hotel in Gerji, Addis Ababa during November and December 2024. What appeared to be a modern, well-kept hotel online turned out to be the opposite in reality. The property is poorly maintained, unclean, and overrun with cockroaches. They were crawling on food, drinks, the bed, the ceiling, the sink, and even the bathtub — including baby cockroaches. Whenever the electricity went out, they would appear instantly, covering the entire room.||I expressed interest in staying longer if they would reduce the rate or move me to the newer-looking building next door, which seems to be around 8 years old. Unfortunately, the manager – an elderly and uncooperative man – was dishonest and dismissive. I was paying $26 per night for the old, rotten room, with a door that barely closed. I showed him live pricing from Agoda, which listed the same room for less, but he kept insisting, “We don’t work with Agoda anymore.”||After two weeks of waiting and being misled, nothing changed. I dislike moving hotels once I’ve settled in, especially since packing and relocating always disrupts my routine, but after four weeks of no improvements, I had no choice but to leave.||Also, the location is misleading. Online it says the hotel is in Bole, but it’s actually in Gerji — a completely different area.||The only highlight of my stay: The three receptionists were outstanding — polite, respectful, and always stood up to greet me. They are the only reason this hotel deserves any credit.||Bottom Line: Emmad Furnished Hotel is not what it claims to be. It is unhygienic, outdated, and misrepresented online. I strongly do not recommend it.

user_reviews.Name: Leo Kortekaas
user_reviews.Description: Emmad Apartment was my home between November 2024 en mid September 2025. I was very happy with the apartment and all the services received.  Very good price for very good quality.

user_reviews.Name: Yoktan Al
user_reviews.Description:
I stay here for almost 3weeks. In the beginning they put me the nicest possible room they have. It has small seating area with TV that doesn’t have internet and jacuzzi that I have never ever used. I am not sure if it work. However, I washed my son in there so it leaks. Another reason is pool have loud music my room had pool view I believe sliding door that face the pool is not sound proof door. I felt like am in the pool with loud noise and grown ladies trying to learn swimming and screaming every second. Was disturbing especially if you take a nap during day time.

There reason I know this hotel was because family members stay here, and told me price they have payed. I cake to check-in each employee at the front desk told me different prices. Only one I could trust at the desk was Sara. Yetmwerk will call you 11pm 5pm by local time to tell you something. I found it very unprofessional considering I have a baby.

I had nice cleaning ladies especially Tigist I think is her name. One of the bell men try to rip us of when we order beer. He try to make 25birr per bottle. We understand make 5-10 a bottle but 25 each is just unacceptable. When we say take it he say ok 70. One think I learn is you can’t trust anyone.

The hotel is very old I change cause spending 600-700 extra for jacuzzi was waste. I was shocked by the room I change to . It was very old mold on wall bathroom sealing want to fell down and bad smell from bathroom.

It’s bit expensive for what you get. They try to say exchange rate is low so you getting cheap rooms, but you can find that price rooms downtown Bole. Only reason I stay was cause they have full kitchen. That was convenient for me with baby.

Breakfast is included however, it’s very small portion most of all tasteless. If you doing breakfast you might as well make it flavorful. I would advise manger to taste the breakfast. Egg taste is water. Chechebsa never seen one like it in Ethiopia. I stop ordering breakfast I get extra coffee instead of my breakfast. Cause their coffee cups are macchiato cups. Only food I enjoyed was shawarma best in Addis I would say.

There is one lady at the restaurant didn’t get her name very unhappy arguing abt everything unwelcoming personality from all stuff.

Location isn’t bad it’s close to everything.

They are renovating so I hope they will improve in the rooms condition and some customer service there is definitely room for growth.

Over all my stay was okay, I felt welcomed, and safe.

user_reviews.Name: Rediet A
user_reviews.Description:
NEVER STAY HERE. Came to get a room. Got threatened by the very drunk son of the owner (I'm assuming) who was insulting me from the beginning. Staff on the inside did nothing to stop him. Had to call the police.
SYAY AWAY

user_reviews.Name: janev436
user_reviews.Description: Great place to stay. Good room, service and food. Reasonable price ($50, cdn).|They were there to pick us up at the airport. Emmad is 10 minutes from Bole airport. the staff was helpful. Free breakfast, and laundry. The room was quiet and spacious. The bed was comfortable and bathrooms are clean and roomy.

user_reviews.Name: Aayana - Finance
user_reviews.Description:
I have stayed over here on 15 Dec 24 and I must say this is very bad hotel in Addis Ababa actually in room there was so many cockroach 🪳🪳🪳 and service is very bad when I called reception to ask about my utility they said there is no Utility like I wanted to take toothbrush and toothpaste, shampoo, body lotion cream but directly said no even you will stay in normal guest house in Addis Ababa they will give you all the services. Unfortunately I have to say this is very bad bad bad hotel.
Thank you

user_reviews.Name: I Faisal
user_reviews.Description:
The hotel in general is very good
I wonder about the people who leave bad comments about the hotel It needs some minor repairs and changes
But it is very comfortable and the staff are very helpful
Starting from the restaurant, reception, cleaners, and hotel manager, they are all helpful and welcoming to visitors.
Thank you Imad Hotel and thank you Ethiopia ♥️
We will come back to you again soon ♥️

Faisal @ Abo Faisal

user_reviews.Name: T. GeBrim
user_reviews.Description:
The building itself looks old and kind of shabby due to its age.
They offer a special rate for long stays, including breakfast, laundry service, and a gym.
Considering the price, it's not bad.

# Addis Ababa # Ethiopia

title: Haikan Hotel | Piazza | ኃይካን ሆቴል | ፒያሳ
address: 2PMW+8J8 Haikan Hotel | Piazza | ኃይካን ሆቴል | ፒያሳ, Near Yekebele, Wawel St, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

owner.name: Haikan Hotel | Piazza | ኃይካን ሆቴል | ፒያሳ (Owner)

user_reviews.Name: Anwar Nasir
user_reviews.Description: A good hotel to stay . The service is good . And the price per night is fair . They offer free breakfast . The only issue i got was dinner is not available after 8:00 night idk why. So u need to order before it gets late. Other than that it was nice

user_reviews.Name: JaneTeesalu
user_reviews.Description: The hotel is quite nice. 30 USD rooms (rooms that are on the third floor) are nice and clean. Though some rooms have some problems, for example in one room the bathroom door did not shut and water was leaking. But we were able to change the room, which was good. ||Rooms with balcony are a bit noisier (due to Fruit market next door), though clean, with comfy beds and hot water. ||Breakfast is a buffee – quite good selection. But as we stayed for 5 nights, then after 3rd morning we had enough of that food. ||||As we stayed quite a few nights we asked for discount, but instead got two free shuttles early in the morning to Meskel Square, which was a good deal for us. Saved us few hundred birrs.||||Wifi is only working in the restaurant area, though they claim that in the rooms as well. Maybe by now it is working, but in the beginning of April, when we were staying there it was not working. ||||Would go back!

user_reviews.Name: beddat
user_reviews.Description: Rooms are spacious, Beds are comfortable, Staff responsive and polite, Shower/bath tub and toilet very clean, All of this at affordable rates for a traveller. However, there are no small fridges in the rooms so you may not access that cold drink in the wee hours of the night. And i could not use their wifi.

user_reviews.Name: NnennaWestAfrica
user_reviews.Description: It was the taxi driver from the airport who told me he will take  me to the hotel. There was a UN summit in town and most middle-class hotels were booked full. I called to ask if they had wifi, hot water and breakfast and they said yes. I paid less than 50$ and the food was really good. I will tell you same thing the driver told me: dont waste your money, sleep at Haikan and you will be fine.

user_reviews.Name: valerie224
user_reviews.Description: The price was right, but the room did not look clean.  Found one roach in the bathroom.  No shower curtain, so had to take shower kneeling down in bathtub.  Front desk staff was not friendly or helpful. Even though signs said they take credit cards, I had to go find a bank to get cash.  ||Breakfast (included with room) and lunch in the restaurant were good -- Western and Ethiopian food.  But they actually ran out of breakfast half way through one morning because there were more guests than the day before.

user_reviews.Name: Abiy-TOH
user_reviews.Description: This hotel is cheap hotel i meant, it is fair it is less 30USD. Any local can stay here see the hotel and Hospitality. Good breakfast relative to the price the service also good and the food is good. the Hotel is usually prepare wedding and Downtown area of around Atikilt tera(Merkato). Ato Messay is Committed to the Hotel as A GM. Keep it up! Hope i will come back.

user_reviews.Name: Mal333
user_reviews.Description: We were booked into this hotel when attended a conference and at that time the public areas and our room were clean and tidy. We didn't eat at the hotel so cannot comment on the restaurant or breakfast mostly because we left early each morning and came back late. It was located in a busy area but didn't have great business service so we tended to go to a large international hotel to use the internet and photocopy etc.

user_reviews.Name: tomaskotouc
user_reviews.Description: I think it is good choice between medium budget Addis hotels. Location can not be better, Tomoca Coffee, Taitu restaurant and Museum are in walking distance. Reception 24 hours, spacy clean room and quite rich breakfest. Bathroom OK, hot water OK and wifi free in room, good signal and surprisingly quick.

title: Sapphire Addis Hotel
address: Namibia St, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
description: Polished rooms, suites & apartments with balconies, plus 2 restaurants, a fitness centre & a spa.

user_reviews.Name: Blen Gashaw
user_reviews.Description: I had a really nice stay at this hotel. Everything was clean and comfortable, and the overall atmosphere was welcoming. The front desk staff were great especially Edom, who was very helpful, kind, and professional.

user_reviews.Name: N8764LKannal
user_reviews.Description: Very convenient to major shops, Airport etc. Calm environment (with the exception of smokers at the corner of the reception) , big rooms at an affordable prices. Fantastic and high level of customer care services offered by most beautiful and angel like ladies at the reception. Prompt and satisfactory room and meal services. Injera!!!!!!

user_reviews.Name: Trip.com Member
user_reviews.Description: We had a wonderful experience during our stay. The hotel was exceptionally clean, and the staff were warm and welcoming throughout. We were especially impressed by the team who served us breakfast and provided room service. The women, including Melat, were incredibly kind and friendly — starting our mornings with her bright smile truly made our stay even more enjoyable.

user_reviews.Name: Peter D'Agostino
user_reviews.Description: Highly impressed by Anna on the desk. She explained a misunderstanding on my part to me and my wife in a highly professional and caring manner. Top marks for her caring empathy. Always beautiful rooms in a spacious and professional environment. A great option when considering a stay in Addis.

user_reviews.Name: peterdK8373KO
user_reviews.Description: In the end, everything was handled in a highly professional manner by the hardworking hotel staff after a slight misunderstanding on my part. They do great rooms here, spacious, clean, affordable, and this is a great option for a wonderful hotel to stay in in Central Addis. It's also quiet and relaxing, and they respect guest's needs for privacy. Top establishment.

user_reviews.Name: Betelihem Love
user_reviews.Description: The hotel is very clean and respectful, and you can easily walk to the Ethiopian Orthodox Church. There are also several shopping centers within walking distance, and the area is truly beautiful at night. I highly recommend this place.

user_reviews.Name: Andy Loke
user_reviews.Description:
My a 9-day-stay was absolutely outstanding! The hotel itself is beautiful, with elegant Ethiopian decor and spotless rooms. But what truly made my experience unforgettable was the incredible staff, mission warm, attentive, and always going above and beyond.
A truly special thanks to the exceptional hospitality of the hotel and the wonderful staff at the café lounge. Every morning, I was greeted with warm smiles and impeccable service, ensuring my breakfast experience was nothing short of delightful. The attention to detail, delicious food, and genuine kindness made each day start on a perfect note.
Ms.Melat Girma and the team,  your dedication truly shines. 👍🏻 keep the best always with you.

user_reviews.Name: Ethiopia Hasme
user_reviews.Description:
We have traveled to Addis for a month and stayed at sapphire Addis for a week. Malat made our stay exceptionally excellent! We will stay in this hotel just for her hospitality. Safe location, clean rooms, great price!!

Ask for Melat ( guest relations) when you come to sapphire.

Highly room mended this hotel!

title: Bellevue Hotel And Spa
address: Megenagna, Addis Ababa 1000, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: zeyneba khelil
user_reviews.Description:
had an excellent 2-day stay at this hotel. From the moment I arrived, the reception staff were welcoming and efficient, making check-in smooth and pleasant.
The customer service throughout my stay was exceptional friendly, attentive, and always ready to help. The decor was beautifully assembled.
The food service was also top-notch. Meals were delicious and well-presented, and I especially want to highlight the dining room waiter, who was incredibly courteous and professional, adding to the overall dining experience.
Overall, it was a wonderful stay. Highly recommend for anyone looking for great service, comfort, and a well-designed space.

user_reviews.Name: E K
user_reviews.Description:
This hotel was a huge disappointment. The bathroom smell was unbearable and spread into the bedroom. The TV didn’t work, the wall light only worked partially. Most power sockets were damaged with exposed wires, which felt unsafe.
The food was terrible and made me sick for few days, the steam and sauna are only symbolic. The temperature cannot be controlled, and it becomes so hot that you can’t stay inside for even two minutes. Overall, the hotel is unsafe  unhealthy. I do not recommend staying here for any one.

user_reviews.Name: Adnan Shemsedin
user_reviews.Description:
⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️⭐️ Absolutely Exceptional Stay at Bellevue Hotel & Spa!

From the moment we arrived, everything about Bellevue Hotel and Spa felt special. The atmosphere was calm and welcoming, the rooms were spotless and beautifully designed, and every detail showed real care and attention.

But what truly made our stay unforgettable was the staff. The staff went above and beyond to make us feel comfortable and valued, always smiling, always ready to help.

A special mention goes to Nohamin at the reception,  she was incredibly kind, professional, and attentive. Her warm welcome and genuine hospitality set the tone for our entire stay. She truly represents the heart of this hotel!

Thank you, Bellevue Hotel and Spa, for such an amazing experience. We’ll definitely be back and recommend it to anyone looking for comfort, elegance, and exceptional service

user_reviews.Name: Eyoas Fikeru
user_reviews.Description:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
We had our wedding day groom and groomsmen retreat at Bellevue Hotel and Spa, and it was absolutely wonderful! The Moroccan bath was a unique experience with special herbs and ingredients that left us feeling refreshed. The Swedish massage was deeply relaxing, and they even offered complimentary juice and refreshments. The staff were professional and attentive, and the spa’s atmosphere and view are unlike any other. Highly recommended for anyone looking for a truly special experience!

user_reviews.Name: Sheen
user_reviews.Description: I advice not using their spa services- mould odour in one of the steam rooms when I was here a few days ago. Today I went to do my nails and ended up with mild burns on my skin as a corrosive gel remover was slapped around my fingers not to mention I was left with jaggedy and damaged nails. Customer service 0/10. Beneath the venear of elegance it's tacky and low-value with a high price (esp. for local prices)

user_reviews.Name: Enku
user_reviews.Description: We stayed for a week and accommodation was great ,with good breakfast and complementary steam sauna and gym access. The spa looks amazing and has cave like structure making it unique in town. Tbe gym is amazing has lots of new equipments and friendly staff.

user_reviews.Name: Woubakal Tesfaye
user_reviews.Description: I booked a cold plunge a day before my visit on Saturday, thinking everything would be set up when I arrived. But when I got there, they weren’t ready at all. It just made me wonder what the point of booking in advance is if the place isn’t prepared by the time the appointment starts. The staff were polite, but the whole experience felt unorganized and disappointing.

user_reviews.Name: Mercy
user_reviews.Description: I booked a room for stay at the Bellevue hotele and this is what I got on the bed and floor. Prior to that I was changed the first room because of the shower not working properly. I took a picture of this and went down to the reception to show the issue to them immediately they called some one took my phone saw the pictures and deleted it from my phone with out my knowledge. I recovered the pictures from recently deleted and sharing them here. I went out from the hotel without no refund with in 20 minutes of booking! It’s a shameful service and experience I really don’t know what to say. I wish I had seen the hotel reviews before booking.

title: Sun view catering and Events
address: Namibia St, Addis Ababa 1000, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: negalign gezahegn
user_reviews.Description:
Sun View Catering and Events exceeded all of our expectations for our special event. From start to finish, the experience was flawless. The team was incredibly professional, attentive, and detail-oriented. They took the time to understand our vision and turned it into a reality.

Sun View Catering and Events helped make our special occasion memorable and stress-free. We highly recommend their services to anyone looking for a top-tier catering and events company. Thank you for making our day truly unforgettable!

user_reviews.Name: Barnabas Mekonnen
user_reviews.Description: I have had the opportunity to experience many hotels recently, but your service is truly impeccable. Although I did not experience the room service, I have heard from my colleague that it was both comfortable and exceptional. I would like to express my sincere gratitude to the remarkable individual who serves us with a smile and great pleasure; he is truly outstanding. mister negasi.. I have enjoyed all the services provided during my time there. thank you may God bless all of you

user_reviews.Name: haleluya admasu
user_reviews.Description:
An Unforgettable Experience at Sun View Hotel!

I had an absolutely amazing experience at Sun View Hotel! From the moment I arrived, the staff made me feel welcome with their warm hospitality and professionalism. The rooms were spotless, the amenities were top-notch, and the atmosphere was both relaxing and luxurious.

A special shoutout to the manager, Negasi, who went above and beyond to ensure my stay was perfect. His attention to detail, kindness, and dedication to guest satisfaction truly set this hotel apart. Whether it was arranging special requests or simply making sure everything ran smoothly, he made my stay unforgettable.

I highly recommend Sun View Hotel to anyone looking for exceptional service and a memorable stay. I will definitely be coming back!

user_reviews.Name: Tamiru Kebede
user_reviews.Description: Sun View Catering and Events apart was their outstanding service. The staff was friendly, efficient, and went above and beyond to ensure that every aspect of the event ran smoothly. They were always available to assist with any requests and made sure that everything was taken care of seamlessly. THANK YOU IN ADVANCE, WE WILL COME AGAIN

user_reviews.Name: Naol Kebede

user_reviews.Name: riadlani alkei
user_reviews.Description:
J’ai passé un séjour absolument merveilleux dans cette guesthouse à Addis-Abeba ! Tout était impeccable : chambres d’une propreté irréprochable, espaces communs très bien entretenus, et un soin du détail remarquable. Les équipements sont excellents, la literie extrêmement confortable, et la chambre spacieuse et agréable. Le WiFi fonctionnait parfaitement, la vue était magnifique, et le petit-déjeuner délicieux, frais et copieux.

Mais ce qui a vraiment rendu le séjour exceptionnel, c’est la gentillesse et la bienveillance de tout le personnel. Des propriétaires aux réceptionnistes, tout le monde s’est montré incroyablement attentionné. Un immense merci tout particulier à Nehumi, qui a été un véritable ange — douce, attentionnée, et tout simplement inoubliable.

Que vous veniez à Addis pour le tourisme ou pour le travail, c’est l’endroit idéal où séjourner. L’établissement est très bien situé, proche de nombreux restaurants, et à une courte distance de l’aéroport. Le rapport qualité-prix est exceptionnel. Je le recommande à 100 % !

PS: les photos sont les vues depuis la chambre (4e étage) et la salle du petit déjeuner (8e étage).

user_reviews.Name: Holger Warnke
user_reviews.Description:
A Safe, Spotless Haven in the Heart of the City

I recently stayed at this guesthouse for several weeks and cannot recommend it enough! From the moment I arrived, I felt completely at ease thanks to its safe environment and immaculate cleanliness. The guesthouse truly has everything you need for a comfortable stay – I never found myself lacking a single amenity.

What sets this place apart is its tranquil inner courtyard, a serene oasis that invites you to unwind. Despite its central location in the bustling city, the courtyard adds a charming, peaceful vibe that makes you forget the urban hustle just steps away. It’s the perfect spot to relax with a book or enjoy a morning coffee.

The staff here are exceptional. Everyone, from the front desk to housekeeping, is friendly, attentive, and genuinely eager to help. A special shout-out to Haile, who went above and beyond with his local tips and warm hospitality. His recommendations for hidden gems in the city were spot-on and made my stay even more memorable.

Overall, this guesthouse strikes the perfect balance between convenience, comfort, and charm. Thank you to the entire team for such a pleasant experience – I’ll absolutely be back on my next visit to the city. If you’re looking for a home away from home, look no further!

user_reviews.Name: Floyd
user_reviews.Description:
Absolutely amazing experience! Haile was an exceptional host—warm, attentive, and incredibly knowledgeable. He and the two young men working with him went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect. Every detail was thoughtfully taken care of, and their hospitality truly exceeded expectations. The rooms were spotless and comfortable, and even when I needed help beyond typical hotel services, they were more than willing to assist.

Haile’s insight into traveling in Ethiopia was invaluable. He guided me on which areas were safe, recommended great local restaurants that were both delicious and affordable, and shared rich, meaningful insights into the everyday lives of the local people. I learned so much about the country’s economic conditions and history through our conversations.

The neighborhood was friendly, welcoming, and felt very safe. Overall, this was not just a stay—it was a deeply enriching experience. I can’t recommend it enough!

user_reviews.Name: Sudays Nuredin (‫السديس‬‎)
user_reviews.Description: Great university. I will speak of every experience. University is great apart from when we leave from library, there is a time schedule and we only go to the dormitory if it is time. Maybe a bridge would be a great idea so students go from library to their dormitories. The lecturers are great. But let me tell you something there is no social life in this university. Students live only for "me, myself and I" ideology. Everyone is on his own, and it is depressing. Even in the dormitory, no one says hi when you enter to you your dormitory. My lecturers too wanted me to return, but I am never going back there unless I change my mind and continue there in the future. You know what is needed here is a social life program. Anthropology, inclusiveness, and critical thinking are good courses for freshman students, but social life skills would have been a better course. Because. A lot of students don't know the basics of social life, and it was really depressing. I had missed orientation, but that wouldn't be a reason for any student to not have a social life at all. Some students don't even know each student in their same classroom. Luckily, I eacaped, or I would have become a drunk man or a drug addict. The cigarette smoke coming from the shower place is so bad that I closed my nose every time. Social life skills should be a course in this university. The good thing is they at least made the green area clean, because at my time it was so dirty and murky. I hope the students become more social because everyone will become an introvert in this university if things don't change.

user_reviews.Name: Nahom Merk
user_reviews.Description: Truth be told, I joined this place thinking it's the best in the country. But there is little to support that reputation. The library is good I guess, but outside that much of it is depressing. There is a mini park with benches (most in need of repair), but there are no fields or courts to enjoy sports or play ball games. No recreation whatsoever. The facilities are no different. There is no water most days (even in toilets), even the toilets themselves are rarely functional. With the exception of a few, most teachers don't deliver high quality lessons and don't care much about the students' performance. They don't even show up most days. I have had better teachers in highschool. The cafeteria is okayish, but the dorm is well below that. It's crowded (8 or more per dorm) and you're considered lucky if you even get a place. I have heard of many low ranking universities outside the capital city with much better dorms than this place. And the registrar and the staff!!!😤😡 Don't get me started on the registrar!!🤮😂 So, long story short, I gave it one star because there isn't a zero star option.

user_reviews.Name: Yalemzewed Girma
user_reviews.Description:
As a current student, I’ve witnessed firsthand the deep-rooted issues within this institution. The administration operates with authoritarian control and widespread corruption. Major decisions that affect students are made without thoughtful analysis or consideration of the consequences. Their leadership is marked by insensitivity, repression, and a blatant disregard for student welfare.
Nepotism is rampant  positions and privileges are often handed out based on personal connections rather than merit, which undermines fairness and excellence. Many staff members display unprofessional attitudes and treat students with hostility or indifference.
Although they claim to be the top institution in Ethiopia, their behavior contradicts that reputation. They reflect a system plagued by corruption, ignorance, and regressive governance. To truly reform this institution, the entire administration must be dismantled and rebuilt with transparency, accountability, and a genuine commitment to education.
Based on my experience, I do not recommend anyone to join this institution.

Addis Ababa University's Natural Sciences Campus is home to the College of Natural and Computational Sciences (CNCS), which offers a wide range of undergraduate and postgraduate programs in the natural sciences and computer science. Academics
The CNCS is a highly respected institution with a strong academic reputation. The college's faculty includes experienced professionals and researchers who are passionate about teaching and scholarship. The curriculum is designed to provide students with a strong foundation in the natural sciences and computer science, as well as the opportunity to specialize in a particular area of interest.
Student life
The Natural Sciences Campus is a vibrant and diverse community with students from all over Ethiopia and beyond. The campus offers a variety of clubs and organizations for students to get involved in, as well as a number of support services to help students succeed academically and personally.
Overall
The Natural Sciences Campus of Addis Ababa University is an excellent choice for students who are interested in pursuing a degree in the natural sciences or computer science. The college offers a high-quality education in a supportive and inclusive environment.

* The campus is home to a number of research facilities, including the Geophysical Observatory and the Institute of Computational Mathematics.

user_reviews.Name: Lakachew Yayeh
user_reviews.Description:
Abune Petros was born in 1892 in a farmer family in the city of Fiche, Ethiopia. At the age of 24 he took the Ethiopian orthodox church oath and became a monk. He grew up and became a well-known teacher around the monasteries in different parts of Ethiopia. His teachings and preaching were very popular and insightful to the people and in 1928 he was nominated to one of four bishops of Ethiopia, with the title and name ABUNE PETROS. He continued to preach the gospel and teach in the churches.

When Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1932, Abune Petros followed with Emperor Haile Selassie and the Ethiopian defense forces to the northern front. He helped the wounded, prayed, consecrated the dead, and preached the Gospel.

ABUNE PETROS executed on 29 July 1936 by the Fascist Italians forces in Ethiopia for publicly condemning colonialism, invasion and massacre. This statue of Abune Petros was raised in Addis Ababa 10 years after his death, as a reminder to future generations of :
•	His strong stand for the truth
•	His unbending courage to stand up against every form of violence against humanity
•	His integrity and commitment not to give in for short-term gain or threat.

user_reviews.Description:
A statue was erected to Menelik II in 1930 at Menelik square in Addis Ababa. It was designed and made by German Architect Curtin Specingler and unveiled in 1931.
The message on the statue reads: "It is not greatness to hail from a prominent family, greatness (triumph) is to contribute something valuable to the motherland."
The message is clearly written to portray the victory of blacks over white opressors--it shows that the color of skin does not make one race superior and another inferior.

Aba Dagnew was Menelik's horse's name. And it stands on its two legs and face to the north--to signify the direction of the battle field.

The place Menelik II Square, formerly Adawa square, was dedicated to erect the statue owing to its location as downtown of the city during the time, Addis Ababa City Administration Culture and Tourism Bureau Intangible Heritages Senior Expert Memhir Mekibib Gebremariam indicates.
Generally, Menelik II statue and Adwa Bridge, around Megenagna, are among the known memorials of the victory of Adwa in Addis Ababa.
Memhir Mekibib underlines the fact that Addis ought to see more memorials to inherit the sprites to posterity and demonstrate the history to visitors.
I share a little you should visit and see our history.

Emperor Menelik II was one of Ethiopia’s greatest leaders, ruling as King and Emperor of Ethiopia from 1889 to 1913. He is a National Hero who gave Ethiopians the freedom and identity we are enjoying.

He was married three times and he had no children with his wives, but several other children by other women that he recognized.

He died in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, on December 12, 1913 at the age of 69. His statue was erected in Addis Ababa in memory of the battle of Adowa. This was the only major battle in the history of Africa, when Emperor Menelik and his army defeated the Italian army.

Addis Ababa fell to Italy in 1936 and was liberated in 1941. The monument at the center of this Square honors the patriots’ fight against fascist Italian invaders, and the victory gained. The monument consists of an obelisk and a relief figure. The obelisk, topped by a Lion of Judah, stands at the center while the relief figure, of Emperor Haile Selassie holding the national flag, encircled the oblisk.

This intersection is surrounded by various significant places like buildings of Ministry of Education, the Parliament, Office of the
Prime Minister, the Palace, Holy Trinity Cathedral, Science College of Addis Ababa University, Menelik II High School and Berhan Ena Selam Printing Press

user_reviews.Name: Mikiyas Melkamu
user_reviews.Description:
The Adwa Victory Center is a project that has been in the works for a few years now, and while it is not yet complete, it is already shaping up to be an incredible destination for anyone interested in learning more about Ethiopia's history.

One of the standout features of the Adwa Victory Center is its focus on the historic Battle of Adwa. This battle was a pivotal moment in Ethiopia's history, and the center is dedicated to educating visitors about the events leading up to the battle, the battle itself, and its aftermath. The center is home to a wealth of artifacts, exhibits, and multimedia installations that bring this moment in history to life in a truly immersive way.

While the Adwa Victory Center is not yet complete, it is clear that a lot of thought and care has gone into its design and construction. The building itself is modern and sleek, with plenty of open spaces and natural light. The center is also fully accessible, with ramps and elevators making it easy for visitors of all abilities to explore the exhibits.

Of course, it is worth noting that the Adwa Victory Center is still a project that is in progress. While there is already plenty to see and do at the center, there are still areas that are under construction or not yet open to the public. However, this should not deter anyone from visiting the center and experiencing all that it has to offer.

if you are interested in learning more about Ethiopia's history, I highly recommend checking out the Adwa Victory Center. While it is still a project that is in progress, it is already shaping up to be an incredible destination that is well worth a visit.

The interior now glows with renewed light—every stained-glass window seems more vibrant, the vaulted ceilings more majestic, and the acoustics have been subtly enhanced to create an atmosphere that’s both serene and powerful. Whether you’re attending a service, a concert, or simply exploring, the space now invites deeper reflection and awe.

Architecturally, the renovations have respected the cathedral’s original Gothic beauty while carefully incorporating contemporary touches that make it feel more accessible and welcoming. The lighting, seating, and layout all reflect thoughtful attention to comfort and inclusivity, without compromising the spiritual grandeur.

The Trinity Cathedral has long been a cornerstone of the community, but this renewal feels like a bold new chapter—one that honors its sacred past while embracing the future with open arms. Simply put, it’s amazing.

user_reviews.Name: Dr. Melaku Taye Amogne
user_reviews.Description:
A Monument Steeped in Ethiopian History and Pride...

The Lion of Judah Monument in Addis Ababa is a profound symbol of Ethiopia's rich history and legacy. As an iconic landmark located in the heart of the city, it is a must-visit for both locals and tourists alike.

As a guy from rural Ethiopia, visiting the Lion of Judah Monument invoked a huge sense of national pride. Its grandeur, which has been masterfully sculpted to embody strength and resilience, is so admirable. The statue stands proudly, exuding a sense of regal dignity that reflects the historical significance of the Lion of Judah in Ethiopian culture and heritage.

The location itself is highly accessible, situated near key landmarks, and easily reachable.
The surrounding area is well-maintained, providing a serene environment for reflection and admiration of the monument. The towering bank headquarters, the distinguished National Theatre, and the charming old Ethiopia Hotel, create a beautiful and historic setting for the monument. This juxtaposition of modern and historical architecture adds to the epic ambiance, highlighting the monument's significance amidst the bustling and dynamic cityscape...

Furthermore, the Lion of Judah Monument serves as an excellent backdrop for photography, with its striking design and the surrounding landscape creating picturesque scenes. It is a perfect spot to capture memorable moments and appreciate the artistic craftsmanship of the statue.

Highly recommended for anyone looking to connect with Ethiopia's storied past and its vibrant present.

user_reviews.Name: fitse wako
user_reviews.Description:
The Lion of Judah Monument in Addis Ababa is one of Ethiopia’s most iconic landmarks, symbolizing the country’s strength, pride, and rich heritage. Located near the National Theatre, the statue holds deep historical and cultural significance, representing the Solomonic dynasty and Ethiopia’s identity as an uncolonized nation.

The monument itself is beautifully crafted, with the lion standing tall on a pedestal, crowned and holding a cross, which adds to its regal and spiritual symbolism. It is not just a work of art but also a powerful reminder of Ethiopia’s resilience and unity.

The surrounding area can be busy, but the monument remains a striking and memorable spot for visitors. It’s a popular stop for history enthusiasts, photographers, and anyone wanting to experience a piece of Ethiopia’s national pride.

Overall, the Lion of Judah Monument is a must-see for anyone visiting Addis Ababa. It’s more than just a statue—it’s a cultural emblem that carries the spirit and story of Ethiopia.

The combination of the intricate craftsmanship and majestic stature of the statue makes it a must-see for anyone visiting Ethiopia. Whether you are a history buff or someone simply wanting to experience some of Ethiopia's rich culture, the Lion of Judah Monument will not disappoint.

user_reviews.Name: ኢትዮጵያዊ
user_reviews.Description: The Imperial Palace was begun as a house on a hill built for Empress Taitu who would visit the hot mineral springs at Felweha, a short distance away. The area was named Addis Ababa by the Empress, and a town grew rapidly around the house of the Empress. In 1886, the capital of the Empire was moved to this site from Mt. Entoto, and Taitu's husband, Emperor Menelik II rebuilt the house as his primary Palace. Over the years the Palace was added to and expanded, to include a multitude of buildings of various sizes and functions in a large wooded compound. The Imperial Palace served as the official Palace even after Emperor Haile Silassie I moved his primary residence out to the Guenete Leul Palace in 1932, and it remained the official seat of the Monarchy until the revolution of 1974. The Marxist military dictatorship (known as the Derg) that overthrew the Imperial Government in September 1974 continued to use the Palace as it's official seat of government. The Derg renamed the Palace as the "Grand Palace" but it also used the term Menelik Palace regularly. The extensive wine cellars of the Palace were used to imprison prominent figures of the Imperial government, including male members of the Solomonic Dynasty. It remained the seat of power of the Peoples Republic of Ethiopia when it was proclaimed in 1987 by the Derg, and the current government of the Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia also uses it as it's official seat of power. Emperor Haile Selassie was kept under detention in one of the buildings in the palace compound following his deposal in 1974. He was killed here, and buried secretly on the grounds, a latrine built over the site of his grave. His remains were disintered following the fall of the Derg and he has been reburied. There are three important churches on the grounds of the Palace. The most prominent is the magnificent Ta'eka Negest (Resting Place of Kings) Ba'eta Le Mariam Monastery, with a large Imperial crown atop it's dome, which serves as the mausoleum of Emperor Menelik II, his wife Empress Taitu, and Empress Zewditu, his daughter and eventual successor. The other churches are the Se'el Bet Kidane Meheret Church (Our Lady Covenant of Mercy) and the Debre Mengist St. Gabriel Church. Former President, Lt. Col. Mengistu Haile Mariam converted the house of the Dean of the Ba'eta Le Mariam Monastery, into a large residence for himself, and this building continues to serve as the residence of the Prime Minister of until 2013. This Palace remains the seat of government in Ethiopia, the Menelik Palace has renovated and most part of it has converted to museum and park and open to the public in 2019.

user_reviews.Name: Stacey Trock
user_reviews.Description:
Where else in the world can you see Lucy, our oldest ancestor? 💕🇪🇹 Only in Ethiopia!

I can not recommend this gem of a museum enough. I'm a lover of natural history museums, and this has the most comprehensive collection of human evolution fossils I've ever seen. It was sheer joy.

Plus, Ethiopian history as well. ❗ Foreigners may be surprised at the depth of Ethiopian history. When Romans were trading, Ethiopians were there with them. Really great artifacts.

💲 Entrance is very inexpensive, we paid 160 birr for two adults and a kid. However, I recommend against the guide. Ours just read the signs aloud and wanted a substantial tip (honestly, I've never had someone tell me the tip I offered wasn't enough, he was only happy with 5 times the entrance fee)

A must-see in Addis!

user_reviews.Name: Ezaldeen Nouraldaim
user_reviews.Description:
The National Museum of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa offers a fascinating look into the country’s rich history and culture. Highlights include the famous Lucy fossil, ancient artifacts, royal treasures, and traditional art. The museum is well organized, and the staff and guides are knowledgeable and friendly.
Overall, it’s an educational and highly recommended place to visit in Addis Ababa.

user_reviews.Name: Scott Forler
user_reviews.Description:
Should be one of the first things to do when you arrive in Ethiopia/Addis Ababa. All informational displays are in English. Upstairs it gives a great overview of the history of Ethiopia going back to 1,000 years BCE covering Ethiopian Antiquity, Christian Kingdoms, Ethiopian Sultantes, and Megalithic Societies. Not a huge display but supported with artifacts and photos of actual sites. Also maps of locations of churches and fossils across Ethiopia. Plenty to see in a day.
Downstairs is the famous Lucy skeleton, both reconstructed and the partial skeleton pieces found. Plenty of information about the origins of our species and some interesting fossils of native animals.

user_reviews.Name: Abraham Yohannes
user_reviews.Description: I really enjoyed my visit to the National Museum of Ethiopia. It was incredible to see  Lucy and other ancient human fossils up close such a powerful reminder of Ethiopia’s place in human history. The museum also has a great collection of royal artifacts, traditional clothing, art, and cultural items that give a strong sense of the country’s heritage. It’s a meaningful and worthwhile experience overall.

يعد The Skyscraper Tower واحدًا من أبرز المعالم الحديثة التي تجسد جمال العمارة وجرأة التصميم في آنٍ واحد. عند الوصول إلى البرج، يلفت الانتباه أولًا شكله المهيب وارتفاعه الشاهق الذي يمنح الزائر إحساسًا بالفخامة والعظمة. تصميمه الخارجي يتميز بمزيج أنيق من الزجاج والحديد، ما يعكس الضوء بشكل مذهل ويعطي المبنى حضورًا بصريًا قويًا سواء في النهار أو عند إضاءته ليلًا.
من الداخل، البرج لا يقل إبهارًا؛ فالمساحات الواسعة والتشطيبات الفاخرة تعكس مستوى راقٍ من الجودة. يوجد فيه مجموعة متنوعة من المرافق، من مطاعم راقية تقدم أطباقًا عالمية بإطلالة بانورامية على المدينة، إلى مقاهٍ هادئة مثالية للاسترخاء أو الاجتماعات الودية. كما يضم مناطق مخصصة للتسوق الفاخر مع علامات تجارية عالمية، مما يجعله مقصدًا متكاملًا للزوار.
أكثر ما يميز The Skyscraper Tower هو منصة المراقبة في الأدوار العليا، حيث يمكن للزائر الاستمتاع بمشهد ساحر يطل على المدينة من ارتفاع شاهق. المنظر يعطي شعورًا بالتحرر والانبهار، خصوصًا عند غروب الشمس أو في ساعات الليل عندما تتلألأ الأضواء.
من ناحية الخدمات، التنظيم داخل البرج مميز، والمصاعد سريعة وآمنة، والموظفون ودودون ويحرصون على تقديم المساعدة للزوار. الأجواء العامة تجمع بين الحداثة والراحة، مما يجعله مكانًا مثاليًا لقضاء الوقت سواء للسياحة أو للأعمال.
باختصار، The Skyscraper Tower ليس مجرد برج شاهق، بل تجربة متكاملة تمزج بين العمارة العصرية والرفاهية والأنشطة المتنوعة، ويستحق أن يكون وجهة أساسية لكل من يبحث عن المتعة والإبهار في قلب المدينة.

user_reviews.Name: Omo Culture Ethiopian Tours
user_reviews.Description:
Historical and Cultural Significance

1. Symbol of the Ethiopian Monarchy:

The Lion of Judah is a symbol of the Ethiopian monarchy, especially associated with the Solomonic dynasty, which claimed descent from King Solomon and the Queen of Sheba.

Emperors of Ethiopia, including Haile Selassie I, used the Lion of Judah as a royal emblem. It represented strength, legitimacy, and divine right to rule.

user_reviews.Name: A. Agena
user_reviews.Description:
The monument of the Lion of Judah is a statue of the Lion of Judah, symbol of Ethiopian Emperors and located in the square of the railway station in Addis Ababa, and marks the end of Winston Churchill Avenue.
The sculpture of the Lion of Judah, in gilded bronze, is placed on a black granite pedestal decorated with relief portraits of Menelik II, Haile Selassie I, Zewditu, and ras Makonnen Wolde Mikael. The work was made by the French sculptor Georges Gardet in 1930, on the occasion of the coronation of Emperor Hailé Selassié on November 2,1930.

title: Ethiopian Science Museum
address: 15/16, Ethiopia

user_reviews.Name: ZEMEN
user_reviews.Description:
Very nice and modern museum. It shows Ethiopia’s future plans using technology in areas like agriculture, aviation, and more, displayed on big screens. It takes about 30–40 minutes to walk through and take photos.

One suggestion: the entrance and exit should be separate, and the ticket system needs improvement. Online ticket booking (like Telebirr) would reduce crowding.
Overall, a great and inspiring place to visit.

user_reviews.Name: Ludo Keeris
user_reviews.Description: Very interseting exhibition on science. Well made with subjects that gets you thinking, like AI, global warming or water management. All in different sections. Some interactive options, also for kids (6+). The building itself is impressive also. Only at the end is a little horeca, that could be a little more. Staff is friendly. Admission (2025) is 400 ETB for adults and 200 ETB for kids

user_reviews.Name: Lindsay Harkness
user_reviews.Description:
Entrance off Menelik II Road. Entrance ticket 400 Birr for museum, to watch a film in The Dome is extra (around the back).  Very interesting technology and AI displays, describes the development push currently happening in Addis. Well worth a visit and lots of hands-on activities and games for kids.

Great views of the city from the rooftop on a clear day!

user_reviews.Name: Suleyman Hassen
user_reviews.Description:
🌍 One of the most futuristic and inspiring places in Addis Ababa!

The Ethiopian Science Museum is a symbol of innovation, progress, and vision for the future. From robotics and AI to space exploration and green technology, every corner of the museum is packed with knowledge and excitement.

🔬 Perfect for students, tech lovers, families, and visitors who want to learn how Ethiopia is stepping into the digital age.

✨ The architecture alone is amazing — modern and smart. The staff were welcoming, and the exhibitions were interactive and easy to understand. I left feeling proud, inspired, and hopeful for Africa’s future in science and technology.

user_reviews.Name: Yalemisew Mintsnote Abgaz
user_reviews.Description:
Not as it was advertised o  social media.
Lots of interesting videos, diagrams, and illustrations. Some of the demos do not work or are closed.

Noticed some plagiarism, failing to cite the sources of the diagrams displayed, and in some cases obvious spelling errors displayed. Not expected from a national museum.

Their website have limited information. This museum can be improved further by making it dynamic than providing static services all the time.

Please change the portrait interactive screens to landscape for the kids to meaningfully interact with them. Aesthetics should match utility!

However, it is a great start and I hope this will improve.

user_reviews.Description: I really appreciate the effort you put into organizing everything neatly and showing us a glimpse into the future and science.I highly recommend visiting this place and you can pay an extra 200 birr to try out Boeing’s virtual plane pilotIng but be warned it’s only available for 15 people on a single day.If you’re interested in trying it out make sure to arrive early

user_reviews.Name: N.S.A
user_reviews.Description:
I got a lotta memories of crossing this bridge as a kid. Now it has been "lavishified" and an artificial rock surface made of resin has been added underneath the bridge.
I don't get it.
Why would you remove actual masonry rocks, that have a historic, even archaeological value, only to replace it with this hollow, morphed, false rock surface made of resin?
And on top of it, add these decorative hooped rings that simulate an enclosure around the pedestrian walkway at the side of the bridge, and use tempered glass as the material of choice for the pedestrian pavement?
Anyway, on the bright side, I stepped on tempered glass for the first time ever. The kids around me were really frightened to walk on glass.

user_reviews.Name: MiTeku Ayene
user_reviews.Description:
Medhane Alem Church — A Sanctuary of Stillness in the Heart of Addis

Medhane Alem Church is one of those rare places where the noise of a city seems to pause the moment you step onto its grounds. During my time in Addis, I would walk there every morning from my hotel—just a short 10-minute stroll—but the effect it had on my mind and spirit lasted the entire day. There was something profoundly grounding about starting my mornings there, watching the city slowly wake up while the church already felt fully alive.

What struck me first was the atmosphere: calm, almost weightless. Despite the constant movement around Addis, Medhane Alem seemed to carry its own rhythm—slower, deeper, deliberate. As soon as I approached its gates, that sense of serenity washed over me. I don’t know if it was the quiet hum of prayers, the soft breeze passing through the courtyard, or simply the presence of something bigger than myself, but it anchored me every morning. It’s one of the few places where you feel both humbled and lifted at the same time.

Architecturally, the church is an incredible representation of Ethiopian Orthodox tradition, capturing both the ancient and the modern in one monumental structure. The scale is grand without being overwhelming; the domes, arches, and carvings all speak to a lineage of craftsmanship and devotion that has shaped Ethiopia’s Orthodox heritage for centuries. Yet there’s a contemporary sharpness to the design—clean lines, bright stone, and an openness that welcomes both worshippers and wanderers alike. It feels timeless, as if the old and the new are in dialogue rather than competition.

The courtyard becomes its own living story. Elderly worshippers making the slow, intentional walk around the church. Children running with a kind of joyous freedom. Pilgrims lighting candles with quiet faces. Priests moving with purpose in their white robes, carrying an air of dignity shaped by tradition and years of service. Even if you don’t understand the language, you understand the devotion. Being there is witnessing faith in its rawest, most unfiltered form.

Inside, the energy shifts—still peaceful, but thicker, heavier with meaning. The chants, the incense, the intricate religious art, the sound of footsteps against polished floors… it creates an atmosphere that feels alive. You don’t need to be Orthodox—or even religious—to appreciate it. The experience itself is spiritual.

What made Medhane Alem special to me wasn’t just its beauty, though it’s undeniably one of the most stunning churches in Addis. It was the feeling. The grounding. The everyday reminder that stillness can be found in the middle of a bustling capital. For those ten minutes walking back to my hotel, I always felt lighter, as if the world made more sense after stepping inside.

If you’re visiting Addis, go early in the morning. Walk the grounds. Sit for a moment. Let the quiet stretch out around you. Medhane Alem isn’t just a landmark—it’s a place the soul recognizes before the mind does.

user_reviews.Description:
Overview

Name: Shola Market (also called Megenagna Shola Gebeya)

Location: Shola area, Yeka Sub-City, Addis Ababa, Ethiopia

Type: Open-air market

What You Can Find

Shola Market offers a wide variety of goods, including:

Clothing & Shoes: Both traditional Ethiopian attire and modern styles

Textiles & Fabrics: Locally made cotton (shemma) and imported fabrics

Food Items: Spices, grains, fruits, vegetables, meat, and dairy products

Handicrafts & Souvenirs: Traditional jewelry, baskets, and household goods

Household Items: Furniture, kitchen utensils, and electronics in some areas

Atmosphere

It’s a bustling local market, less touristy than Merkato but still full of color and energy. You’ll hear lively bargaining, see vibrant displays, and experience the authentic daily life of Addis Ababa residents.

Accessibility

Easily reachable by taxi or minibus from most parts of the city.

Located close to Megenagna, a major transport hub.

Parking is available, but often crowded.

Tips for Visitors

Best to visit in the morning for fresh produce.

Bargaining is expected—prices are negotiable.

Keep an eye on your belongings, as it can get crowded.

Great spot for experiencing local life and culture.

user_reviews.Name: Markus Haile
user_reviews.Description:
This is a very important museum that highlights a very sad part in the Ethiopian history. Most doesn’t know much what happened behind the iron curtain, even less when it comes to the African curtain.

Ethiopia is still suffering from the Derg years, dark times and lots of human tragedies. The museum covers what led up to the revolution, how Menge took power and the red terror that followed. It gives you the basics but I suggest you do some reading before you come here since the museum far from covers the lot. I wouldn’t call this museum complete; it is very small with not that many exhibitions but it does give a somehow ok insight.

Reason for only three stars, the building which was built by one of the best contractors is in badly need of maintenance, at least the statue outside, the sign of it is hardly readable, shame really. There´s also a broken minibus parked in the museum for no reason (lack of funding they said). No entrance fee but a donation is highly expected, also the guide will try to shake some extras and promoting himself as a tour guide for you to buy his services. I know salaries have lots to ask for but expected some more professionalism. The museum offers some basic printed books which are very interesting.

More resources should be put into this place since its an important part of Ethiopian history, museum it’s not very old either but continuing in this direction it will be a shackle within some years which is sad, worth a visit, definitely, honour those that are not with us anymore. Long live the Empire.

user_reviews.Name: Mikiyas Melkamu
user_reviews.Description: The Red Terror Martyrs’ Memorial Museum is a powerful reminder of the struggles endured by those under oppressive regimes. The exhibits document the impact of the Red Terror in Ethiopia and provide a sobering look at the unconscionable acts of violence and injustice inflicted upon citizens of Ethiopia. The museum is incredibly poignant and serves as a platform to deliver an important message: those who have suffered under a violent government have a voice and it must be heard. Additionally, it is free to enter, making it an accessible place to learn and remember. Apart from the physical museum, there is much to be learned from discussions with locals. It is important to gain insight from those who lived through the Red Terror and can provide multiple perspectives on the political situation at the time. It is equally as important to speak to the younger generations and understand their views of life today in comparison. The museum, plus conversations with those affected, offer a deeper understanding of the past and the present.

user_reviews.Name: Amanu R
user_reviews.Description:
La Gare is a historic train station located in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. It was built in 1929 during the Italian occupation of Ethiopia and served as a major transportation hub for the country's railway system. The station's unique architecture, featuring a mix of Italian and Ethiopian design elements, has made it an important landmark in the city.
However, over the years, the station has fallen into disuse and disrepair. The decline of Ethiopia's railway system and the rise of alternative modes of transportation have led to a decrease in passenger traffic at La Gare. The station's once-grand building now stands empty and neglected.
Moreover, adaptive reuse would preserve and revive La Gare's historical and architectural significance while giving it a new lease on life. The station would become a symbol of Addis Ababa's past and present, a reminder of the city's rich cultural heritage and a hub of activity and community.

user_reviews.Name: Henokabba
user_reviews.Description:
The Ethio-Korean War Veteran Memorial Park is more than just a place of remembrance; it is a powerful tribute, a peaceful green space and a symbol of Ethiopia’s proud international legacy. Nestled along the beautifully developed Addis Abeba River Side Project, the park seamlessly blends history, nature and community life.

Monument of Honor
At the heart of the park stands a solemn monument dedicated to the more than 100 Ethiopian soldiers who fought valiantly in the Korean War. The design is both respectful and commanding, honoring the bravery and sacrifice of those martyrs who represented Ethiopia on the global stage. It offers a poignant reminder of Ethiopia’s contribution to global peace and solidarity.

Clean & Green Landscape
The park itself is immaculately maintained, with lush greenery, well-kept lawns and shaded pathways. It provides a quiet escape from the city bustle; ideal for peaceful reflection, reading or a relaxing walk. Benches and sitting areas are thoughtfully placed; making it welcoming for all ages.

Impactful Museum
One of the standout features is the on-site museum which houses emotional and educational exhibits. Through photos, artifacts, uniforms & well-documented stories, it depicts a vivid picture of the Ethiopian battalion’s journey and heroism in Korea. The curation is simple yet impactful; engaging both locals and international visitors alike.

Family-Friendly Environment
Families will appreciate the children’s playground which is integrated into the park without disrupting its solemn atmosphere. It is a great way to introduce younger generations to Ethiopia’s history while also giving them space to enjoy the outdoors.

Riverside Integration
Now part of the Addis Abeba River Side Project, the park feels even more vibrant and accessible. The river-side walking paths, artistic installations and nearby cafes add an urban charm while preserving the park’s dignity and purpose.

The Ethio-Korean War Veteran Memorial Park is a must-visit site in Addis Ababa. Whether you come to honor the fallen, explore the museum or simply enjoy the peaceful surroundings, the experience is enriching. It beautifully captures the balance between remembrance and renewal; a true model for how public memorials can serve both historical and community purposes.

Highly recommended for history lovers, families, students and children alike.

user_reviews.Name: Manuel Jesús Padilla Domínguez
user_reviews.Description:
The Heart of Ethiopia Has a Name: Yihun and Sisay

We spent 20 days traveling through Ethiopia — a country as fascinating as it is complex. But what truly made this journey unforgettable was experiencing it alongside Yihun and Sisay. They weren’t just our guide and driver; they were the soul of our trip, and choosing to travel with them was the best decision we could have made.

Yihun is the kind of guide every traveler dreams of: deeply professional, always attentive, and with a calm presence that makes you feel safe from the first moment. His knowledge of the country — its history, its culture, its people — is vast, and he shares it with passion and respect. He made sure every single day went smoothly, shielding us from scams and inconveniences, and ensuring we could simply enjoy and learn. But above all, he’s a kind, generous, and honest human being. I brought back many memories from Ethiopia, but his friendship is by far the most precious.

Sisay, our driver, was another gift. In a country where traffic rules seem to be merely suggestions, he was a constant source of safety and peace of mind. He drives skillfully and carefully, always with a big smile on his face. He kept us entertained during long drives, shared the music and rhythms of each region, and was equally curious and open to hearing music from our own country. His joy, warmth, and attentiveness made him much more than a driver — he became a beloved travel companion.

Ethiopia can be a challenging destination, but thanks to them, it felt welcoming, human, and full of light. They showed us their land with pride, dedication, and a level of humanity that’s rare to find. By the end of the trip, saying goodbye brought a lump to our throats and the certainty that we were leaving behind two real friends.

If you’re thinking of traveling to Ethiopia, do it with them. They are exceptional professionals and even better people. Thanks to Yihun and Sisay, we didn’t just discover a country — we discovered its heart.

user_reviews.Name: geni tsiyon
user_reviews.Description:
We were picked up by our guide (Solomon) at our hotel in Semera and off we went to the first Ertale. During the entire trip Solomon showed us that we is an experienced driver and guide. He showed us the best spots in Danakil Depression & made sure to include us in the decision making of where to go or when to leave. The accommodations was open tents  were amazing. The first night was actually very windy. The other one night were basic camp sites but that was half of the fun. To stay and sleep surrounded by mountains and rivers is equally exciting
Make sure you bring warm clothes as well as a flashlight and a powerbank to be prepared. You can charge your phone often but it is nice to be able to do it in your tent as well if needed.

Do not worry about the quality or quantity of the food because there will be an abundance of food each meal. The chef made excellent meals all day long.

The most important thing during this trip would probably the salt lakes, wow! There were so many and Solomon made sure we saw each and every one of them. You could tell he is an experienced guide by the way the communicated with the others via radio and found every hidding place of the animals. It was very exciting all day long!

Overall this was one of the best experience of my life and I would greatly recommend booking your experience of Danakil Depression with Aman Ethiopia Tours. They are truly the best. I could talk for hours about this trip but I will let my pictures do the rest of the “talking”.

user_reviews.Name: Sabina Wojciechowska
user_reviews.Description:
We had a two-week tailor-made trip organized with Aman Ethiopia Tours and the experience was exceptional from start to finish. The team was highly professional, friendly, and attentive to every detail, and we felt very safe and well taken care of throughout the entire journey. The itinerary they crafted allowed us to experience Ethiopia’s incredible diversity—from the timeless rock-hewn churches of Lalibela and the castles of Gondar to the Blue Nile and Awash Waterfalls, and the beautiful shores of Lake Tana. Each place left a lasting impression, and we truly felt that we were in great hands the whole time.
Highly recommended for anyone looking to explore Ethiopia in an authentic, safe, well-organized, and personal way.

My tour guide Abe reminded me of one of my College History Professors, extremely knowledgeable and passionate about the history of Ethiopia. I did the city tour on day 1, day 2 was given a personal driver to drive me around (had to check out a spa and do some shopping lol), day 3 was just wow, out in the country side visited the amazing Adadi Maryam Rock Hewn Church, Tiya Stele, and the Melka Kunture Archaeological Sites, all were breathtaking experiences!! Thank you Abe and The Aman tour team for helping create a life time memorable experience, looking forward to coming back soon!

user_reviews.Name: Isaac Abre
user_reviews.Description:
Review for the Zoological Natural History Museum, Addis Ababa

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

The Zoological Natural History Museum in Addis Ababa is a hidden gem that offers a fascinating glimpse into Ethiopia's rich biodiversity and natural history. Established in 1955 at the University College of Addis Ababa, it holds the distinction of being the only natural history museum in the country, making it a must-visit for both locals and tourists alike.

Located within the science faculty compound, the museum houses an impressive collection of over 1,100 animal species, showcasing the incredible variety of wildlife found in Ethiopia and beyond. The exhibits are well-organized and informative, providing insights into the ecological significance of each species and their habitats.

During my visit, I was particularly impressed by the attention to detail in the displays, which highlight not only the beauty of the specimens but also the importance of conservation efforts. The museum's knowledgeable staff are passionate about educating visitors, and their enthusiasm truly enhances the experience.

Whether you're a nature enthusiast, a student, or simply curious about Ethiopia's natural heritage, the Zoological Natural History Museum is a fantastic destination. It offers a unique opportunity to learn about the country's wildlife while appreciating the importance of preserving it for future generations.

I highly recommend adding this museum to your itinerary when visiting Addis Ababa. It's a wonderful place to explore, discover, and appreciate the natural wonders of Ethiopia!

user_reviews.Name: Amer Salih
user_reviews.Description:
Addis Ababa museum in Meskel Square is a quiet, small museum located just behind the Red Terror Martyrs Memorial museum. This museum has two entrances, one through the Meskel Square area where you have to pay 20 Ethiopian birr to enter the square itself and then 20 more birr to enter the museum (1 united states dollars ~ 100 Ethiopian birr). The other entrance is near the Red Terror Martyrs Memorial museum where you do not have to pay the 20 Ethiopian birr fee to enter the Meskel Square area (but I highly recommend entering this area because it has lots and lots of activities and food cars).

The museum itself is small with rooms where they display actual royal clothes and artifacts with explanations to everything you see. You'll also get to know much of the history of the city of Addis Ababa (lit; the new flower).

After the rooms of the clothes you get to see photos and weapons (guns, sords and shields) used by the Ethiopian army to defend the city against the Italian colonial army. Also you get to contemplate various coin collections and beautiful artifacts.

After completing the inner rooms of the museum, never forget to check out the art gallery upstairs where they host beautiful paintings and sculptures, some of them for sale. There's also another room just above the museum's rooms where they display many paintings given to the museum.

The place has a nice green area in front of the entrance and a very fancy restaurant outside.
I'd pay the 20 birr for this area by itself cause it's very green and looks right above Meskel Square.

I'd also pay the 20 birr to experience the Meskel Square area and the various entertaining activities there, especially the rental bicycles.

description: Ancient relics, contemporary paintings & the famous fossilized bones of the early hominid Lucy.

user_reviews.Name: Elizabeth “Talatu” Williams
user_reviews.Description:
It was a great experience, should definitely be your first stop when you visit Ethiopia. The museum boasts of rich history and relics including the famous Lucy!

The museum was very clean and aesthetically pleasing. As a tourist, you have to pay 50 birr for the ticket to access the museum. It is so worth it for that cost.

Make sure you go into the museum and take in the experience!

user_reviews.Name: Stacey Trock
user_reviews.Description:
Where else in the world can you see Lucy, our oldest ancestor? 💕🇪🇹 Only in Ethiopia!

I can not recommend this gem of a museum enough. I'm a lover of natural history museums, and this has the most comprehensive collection of human evolution fossils I've ever seen. It was sheer joy.

Plus, Ethiopian history as well. ❗ Foreigners may be surprised at the depth of Ethiopian history. When Romans were trading, Ethiopians were there with them. Really great artifacts.

💲 Entrance is very inexpensive, we paid 160 birr for two adults and a kid. However, I recommend against the guide. Ours just read the signs aloud and wanted a substantial tip (honestly, I've never had someone tell me the tip I offered wasn't enough, he was only happy with 5 times the entrance fee)

A must-see in Addis!

user_reviews.Name: Ezaldeen Nouraldaim
user_reviews.Description:
The National Museum of Ethiopia in Addis Ababa offers a fascinating look into the country’s rich history and culture. Highlights include the famous Lucy fossil, ancient artifacts, royal treasures, and traditional art. The museum is well organized, and the staff and guides are knowledgeable and friendly.
Overall, it’s an educational and highly recommended place to visit in Addis Ababa.

user_reviews.Name: Scott Forler
user_reviews.Description:
Should be one of the first things to do when you arrive in Ethiopia/Addis Ababa. All informational displays are in English. Upstairs it gives a great overview of the history of Ethiopia going back to 1,000 years BCE covering Ethiopian Antiquity, Christian Kingdoms, Ethiopian Sultantes, and Megalithic Societies. Not a huge display but supported with artifacts and photos of actual sites. Also maps of locations of churches and fossils across Ethiopia. Plenty to see in a day.
Downstairs is the famous Lucy skeleton, both reconstructed and the partial skeleton pieces found. Plenty of information about the origins of our species and some interesting fossils of native animals.

user_reviews.Name: Abraham Yohannes
user_reviews.Description: I really enjoyed my visit to the National Museum of Ethiopia. It was incredible to see  Lucy and other ancient human fossils up close such a powerful reminder of Ethiopia’s place in human history. The museum also has a great collection of royal artifacts, traditional clothing, art, and cultural items that give a strong sense of the country’s heritage. It’s a meaningful and worthwhile experience overall.

user_reviews.Name: Mollyn Butaumocho

user_reviews.Name: fitse wako
user_reviews.Description:
The Ethiopian Institute of Financial Studies, under the National Bank of Ethiopia, is a key institution dedicated to building capacity in the country’s financial sector. It plays an important role in training professionals in banking, finance, and economics, helping strengthen Ethiopia’s financial system through knowledge and skills development.

The institute offers well-structured programs, workshops, and seminars that cover a wide range of financial topics, from central banking and monetary policy to modern banking practices. Its curriculum is practical and up to date, aimed at addressing the real needs of Ethiopia’s growing economy.

Participants often appreciate the professionalism of the trainers, the quality of resources, and the supportive learning environment. The institute also provides a space for dialogue and knowledge-sharing among financial experts, which adds to its value.

Overall, the Ethiopian Institute of Financial Studies is a cornerstone for Ethiopia’s financial sector, ensuring that professionals are equipped with the knowledge and expertise to contribute to the country’s economic development
